page: Microsoft Azure D16ds_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. The instance allocates 16 dedicated vCPUs derived from 8 physical cores via two-way multithreading. System memory totals 64.0 GB, representing a standard 1:4 core-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The hardware design incorporates 480 MB of shared L3 cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 48 KB of L1 data cache per core, alongside vector instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX).

Storage architecture is provisioned with 944 GB of direct-attached local NVMe SSD storage suited for high-throughput ephemeral caching and scratch data. Discrete GPU hardware is absent, relying entirely on the central processor for computational tasks. Complimentary public IPv4 addresses are not included with the virtual machine allocation.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-threaded data manipulation, recording 35.66 GB/sec in gzip compression and 14.92 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression, placing it in the top quartile of evaluated instances. Hardware-level matrix acceleration enables 354.35 tokens per second during text generation inference runs on small 135M parameter models. General compute tests, memory bandwidth metrics, and static web serving throughput (30.44 GB/sec) align within standard median baseline performance bands.

The D16ds_v7 offers balanced resource density by packaging dedicated high-frequency CPU cores, integrated NVMe performance, and modern instruction sets into a single configuration. It is well structured for relational database hosting requiring fast local swap space, data compression and transformation pipelines, continuous integration runners, and containerized web application serving.
description: Microsoft Azure D16ds_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine built on an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor clocked at 4.2 GHz. Operating under Microsoft Hyper-V, it provides 16 dedicated vCPUs derived from 8 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled. The configuration is equipped with 64.0 GB of RAM, yielding a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation, and features a 480 MB L3 cache alongside AVX-512 and AMX instruction sets. The server includes 944 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and lacks discrete GPU hardware. Empirical testing reflects upper-quartile execution in single-threaded data compression alongside top-tier text generation on small language models via CPU matrix acceleration. General multi-core processing, static web serving, and database transactions perform within standard median ranges. Given its integrated high-speed local NVMe capacity and balanced resource footprint, the D16ds_v7 is suited for medium-tier database backends, caching nodes, CI/CD build environments, and containerized enterprise applications.
